On 12 October 2015, the court found [Jiang](/wiki/Jiang_Jiemin "Jiang Jiemin") guilty on all counts, including accepting bribes, possessing dark assets, and abusing his power. He was sentenced to 16 years in prison.[[53]](#cite_note-53)

In January 2017, former vice chairman [Liao Yongyuan](/wiki/Liao_Yongyuan "Liao Yongyuan") was sentenced to 15 years in prison for abuse of power and accepting nearly $2 million worth of bribes.[[54]](#cite_note-54)[[55]](#cite_note-55)

1905 magazine advertisement

In 1901, the Quaker Oats Company was founded in [New Jersey](/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") with headquarters in Chicago, by the merger of four [oat mills](/wiki/Rolled_oats "Rolled oats"): the Quaker Mill Company in Ravenna, Ohio, which held the trademark on the Quaker name; the cereal mill in [Cedar Rapids, Iowa](/wiki/Cedar_Rapids,_Iowa "Cedar Rapids, Iowa"), owned by John Stuart, his son [Robert Stuart](/wiki/Robert_Stuart_(businessman) "Robert Stuart (businessman)"), and their partner George Douglas; the [German Mills American Oatmeal Company](/wiki/German_Mills_American_Oatmeal_Company "German Mills American Oatmeal Company") in Akron, Ohio, owned by Schumacher; The Rob Lewis & Co. American Oats and Barley Oatmeal Corporation. Formally known as "Good For Breakfast" instant oatmeal mix. In the same year, the whole merged company was acquired by Crowell, who also bought the [bankrupt](/wiki/Bankrupt "Bankrupt") Quaker Oat Mill Company, also in Ravenna.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

In 1908, Quaker Oats introduced the first in a series of cookie recipes on the box. In 1911, Quaker Oats purchased the Great Western Cereal Company. The iconic cylindrical package made its first appearance in 1915. Later that year, Quaker offered the first cereal box premium to buyers. By sending in one dollar and the cutout picture of the "Quaker Man", customers received a double boiler for the cooking of oatmeal.

In the 1920s, Quaker introduced "Quaker Quick Oats", an early [convenience food](/wiki/Convenience_food "Convenience food"), and also offered a crystal radio set built in the same cylindrical canister as Quick Oats, with the same label, for [US$](/wiki/US$ "US$")1 plus two trademarks cut from Quak

In July 2004, Everton offered Rooney a new five-year contract valued at £50,000 per week,[[61]](#cite_note-61) the most lucrative ever offered by the club.[[62]](#cite_note-62) Amidst increasing speculation linking Rooney with a transfer, Everton chairman [Bill Kenwright](/wiki/Bill_Kenwright "Bill Kenwright") admitted the club's financial situation meant a transfer would "revitalise" the club.[[63]](#cite_note-63) Everton rejected a bid of £20 million from Newcastle,[[64]](#cite_note-64) and Rooney submitted a transfer request on 27 August,[[65]](#cite_note-65) with Moyes saying he would not leave unless the club got the right price for him.[[66]](#cite_note-66) He ultimately signed for [Manchester United](/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") at the end of the month after an initial £20 million deal was reached, with an additional £7 million in contingency payments, with Rooney signing a five-year contract.[[67]](#cite_note-67)[[68]](#cite_note-68) It was the highest fee ever paid for a player under 20 years old; Rooney was still only 18 when he left Everton.[[69]](#cite_note-69) [Sir Alex Ferguson](/wiki/Alex_Ferguson "Alex Ferguson"), then manager of United, said that "There were plenty of eyebrows raised" when he persuaded the club's board of directors to sanction "a multi-million pound" move to try to sign Rooney.[[70]](#cite_note-70) In an appearance on United's official [podcast](/wiki/Podcast "Podcast") in 2020, Rooney revealed Everton had wanted him to sign for [Chelsea](/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") to ensure a bigger transfer fee,[[71]](#cite_note-71) while the mooted transfer to Newcastle would have seen a clause put in place for him to leave after a year to join United.[[72]](#cite_note-72)

> Rooney can do the lot. Eventually he'll have all the United records.

— United legend [Denis Law](/wiki/Denis_Law "Denis Law")

**Luxembourg**,[[a]](#cite_note-10) officially the **Grand Duchy of Luxembourg**,[[b]](#cite_note-11) is a [landlocked country](/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") in [Western Europe](/wiki/Western_Europe "Western Europe"). It is bordered by [Belgium](/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") to the west and north, [Germany](/wiki/Germany "Germany") to the east, and [France](/wiki/France "France") to the south and west. Its capital and most populous city, [Luxembourg City](/wiki/Luxembourg_City "Luxembourg City"),[[10]](#cite_note-12) is one of [the four institutional seats of the European Union](/wiki/Institutional_seats_of_the_European_Union "Institutional seats of the European Union")[[c]](#cite_note-13) and hosts several [EU](/wiki/European_Union "European Union") institutions, notably the [Court of Justice of the European Union](/wiki/Court_of_Justice_of_the_European_Union "Court of Justice of the European Union"), the highest judicial authority in the EU.[[11]](#cite_note-14)[[12]](#cite_note-15)

As part of the [Low Countries](/wiki/Low_Countries "Low Countries"), Luxembourg has [close historic, political, and cultural ties](/wiki/Benelux "Benelux") to [Belgium](/wiki/Belgium "Belgium") and the [Netherlands](/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). [Luxembourg's culture](/wiki/Culture_of_Luxembourg "Culture of Luxembourg"), people, and [languages](/wiki/Languages_of_Luxembourg "Languages of Luxembourg") are greatly influenced by France and Germany: [Luxembourgish](/wiki/Luxembourgish "Luxembourgish"), a Germanic language, is the only recognized [national language](/wiki/National_language "National language") of the [Luxembourgish people](/wiki/Luxembourgers "Luxembourgers") and of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg;[[13]](#cite_note-auto-16)[[14]](#cite_note-17) French is the sole language for legislation; and both languages along with German are used for administrative matters.[[13]](#cite_note-auto-16)

Main article: [*GoldenEye*](/wiki/GoldenEye "GoldenEye")

In 1986, Bond (played by [Pierce Brosnan](/wiki/Pierce_Brosnan "Pierce Brosnan")) and [Alec Trevelyan](/wiki/Alec_Trevelyan "Alec Trevelyan")—agent 006—infiltrate an illicit Soviet chemical weapons facility and plant explosive charges. Trevelyan is shot, but Bond escapes from the facility as it explodes. Nine years later, Bond witnesses the theft by criminal organisation Janus of a prototype [Eurocopter Tiger](/wiki/Eurocopter_Tiger "Eurocopter Tiger") helicopter that can withstand an [electromagnetic pulse](/wiki/Electromagnetic_pulse "Electromagnetic pulse"). Janus uses the helicopter to steal the control disk for the dual GoldenEye satellite weapons, using the GoldenEye to destroy the complex with an electromagnetic pulse; there are two survivors of the attack, the programmers [Natalya Simonova](/wiki/Natalya_Simonova "Natalya Simonova") and Boris Grishenko.

Bond investigates the attack and travels to Russia where he locates Simonova and learns that Trevelyan, who had faked his own death, was the head of Janus. Simonova tracks computer traffic to Cuba and she and Bond travel there and locate Trevelyan, who reveals his plan to steal money from the [Bank of England](/wiki/Bank_of_England "Bank of England") before erasing all of its financial records with the GoldenEye, concealing the theft and destroying Britain's economy. Bond and Simonova destroy the satellite facility, killing Trevelyan and Grishenko in the process.

Further information: [Lists of law clerks of the Supreme Court of the United States](/wiki/Lists_of_law_clerks_of_the_Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Lists of law clerks of the Supreme Court of the United States")

Each Supreme Court justice hires several [law clerks](/wiki/Law_clerk#Federal_clerkships "Law clerk") to review petitions for writ of *[certiorari](/wiki/Certiorari "Certiorari")*, [research](/wiki/Legal_research "Legal research") them, prepare [bench memorandums](/wiki/Bench_memorandum "Bench memorandum"), and draft opinions. Associate justices are allowed four clerks. The chief justice is allowed five clerks, but Chief Justice Rehnquist hired only three per year, and Chief Justice Roberts usually hires only four.[[246]](#cite_note-Peppers2006-246) Generally, law clerks serve a term of one to two years.

The first law clerk was hired by Associate Justice [Horace Gray](/wiki/Horace_Gray "Horace Gray") in 1882.[[246]](#cite_note-Peppers2006-246)[[247]](#cite_note-Weiden2006-247) [Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.](/wiki/Oliver_Wendell_Holmes_Jr. "Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.") and [Louis Brandeis](/wiki/Louis_Brandeis "Louis Brandeis") were the first Supreme Court justices to use recent [law school](/wiki/Law_school "Law school") graduates as clerks, rather than hiring "a [stenographer](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/stenographer#Noun "wikt:stenographer")-secretary".[[248]](#cite_note-Chace2007-248) Most law clerks are recent law school graduates.

The first female clerk was [Lucile Lomen](/wiki/Lucile_Lomen "Lucile Lomen"), hired in 1944 by Justice [William O. Douglas](/wiki/William_O._Douglas "William O. fanoutqa_000345.x:
Continent :: Definitions and application :: chunk_0002
By convention, continents "are understood to be large, continuous, discrete masses of land, ideally separated by expanses of water".[[9]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewis_&_Wigen,_The_Myth_of_Continents199721-9) By this definition, all continents have to be an island of some metric. In modern schemes with five or more recognized continents, at least one pair of continents is joined by land in some fashion. The criterion "large" leads to arbitrary classification: [Greenland](/wiki/Greenland "Greenland"), with a surface area of 2,166,086 square kilometres (836,330 sq mi), is only considered the world's largest island, while [Australia](/wiki/Australia_(continent) "Australia (continent)"), at 7,617,930 square kilometres (2,941,300 sq mi), is deemed the smallest continent.

Earth's major landmasses all have coasts on a single, continuous [World Ocean](/wiki/Ocean#World_Ocean "Ocean"), which is divided into several principal oceanic components by the continents and various geographic criteria.[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-UNAoO-11)

The geological definition of a continent has four criteria: high elevation relative to the ocean floor; a wide range of igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks rich in silica; a crust thicker than the surrounding oceanic crust; and well-defined limits around a large enough area.[[12]](#cite_note-nytimes.com-12)

The teams met again in the [2018 Eastern Conference Semifinals](/wiki/2018_NBA_playoffs "2018 NBA playoffs") as both team advanced from the first round, led by their new draft pick [Jayson Tatum](/wiki/Jayson_Tatum "Jayson Tatum") from Celtics with [Ben Simmons](/wiki/Ben_Simmons "Ben Simmons") and [Joel Embiid](/wiki/Joel_Embiid "Joel Embiid") from 76ers, respectively. **Francis II and I** ([German](/wiki/German_language "German language"): *Franz II*; 12 February 1768 – 2 March 1835) was the last [Holy Roman Emperor](/wiki/Holy_Roman_Emperor "Holy Roman Emperor") as **Francis II** from 1792 to 1806, and the first [Emperor of Austria](/wiki/Emperor_of_Austria "Emperor of Austria") as **Francis I** from 1804 to 1835. He was also [King of Germany](/wiki/List_of_monarchs_of_Germany "List of monarchs of Germany"), [Hungary](/wiki/King_of_Hungary "King of Hungary"), [Croatia](/wiki/List_of_rulers_of_Croatia "List of rulers of Croatia") and [Bohemia](/wiki/List_of_Bohemian_monarchs "List of Bohemian monarchs"), and served as the first president of the [German Confederation](/wiki/German_Confederation "German Confederation") following its establishment in 1815.

The eldest son of future [Emperor Leopold II](/wiki/Leopold_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Leopold II, Holy Roman Emperor") and [Maria Luisa of Spain](/wiki/Maria_Luisa_of_Spain "Maria Luisa of Spain"), Francis was born in [Florence](/wiki/Florence "Florence"), where his father ruled as [Grand Duke of Tuscany](/wiki/List_of_grand_dukes_of_Tuscany "List of grand dukes of Tuscany"). Leopold became Holy Roman Emperor in 1790 but died two years later, and Francis succeeded him. His empire immediately became embroiled in the [French Revolutionary Wars](/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Wars "French Revolutionary Wars"), the first of which ended in Austrian defeat and the loss of the left bank of the [Rhine](/wiki/Rhine "Rhine") to France. After another French victory in the [War of the Second Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_Second_Coalition "War of the Second Coalition"), [Napoleon](/wiki/Napoleon "Napoleon") crowned himself [Emperor of the French](/wiki/Emperor_of_the_French "Emperor of the French"). See also: [Mayor of Islamabad](/wiki/Mayor_of_Islamabad "Mayor of Islamabad"), [Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation](/wiki/Islamabad_Metropolitan_Corporation "Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation"), and [Capital Development Authority (Islamabad)](/wiki/Capital_Development_Authority_(Islamabad) "Capital Development Authority (Islamabad)")

The [Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Administration](/wiki/ICT_Administration "ICT Administration"), generally known as ICT Administration, is the civil administration as well as main law and order agency of the federal capital.

The local government authority of the city is the [Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation](/wiki/Islamabad_Metropolitan_Corporation "Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation") (IMC) with some help from Capital Development Authority (CDA), which oversees the planning, development, construction, and administration of the city.[[55]](#cite_note-TN-60)[[56]](#cite_note-61) Islamabad Capital Territory is divided into eight zones: Administrative Zone, Commercial District, Educational Sector, Industrial Sector, Diplomatic Enclave, Residential Areas, Rural Areas and Green Area.[[57]](#cite_note-Islamabad.com-62) Islamabad city is divided into five major zones: Zone I, Zone II, Zone III, Zone IV, and Zone V. Out of these, Zone IV is the largest in area.[[58]](#cite_note-map-63) Zone I consists mainly of all the developed residential sectors while Zone II consists of the under-developed residential sectors. Each residential sector is identified by a letter of the alphabet and a number, and covers an area of approximately 2 km × 2 km (1+1⁄4 mi × 1+1⁄4 mi). The sectors are lettered from A to I, and each sector is divided into four numbered sub-sectors.[[59]](#cite_note-S._Hull-64)

Avatar (franchise) :: Films :: Avatar 4 (2029) :: chunk_0006
A fourth film is planned for release on December 21, 2029.[[7]](#cite_note-D'Alessandro-7)[[8]](#cite_note-varietyreleasedates-8) Jon Landau said that, due to an eight-year time skip in the first act, a third of *Avatar 4* has already been filmed to account for the aging of the child actors. However, he said that he would not continue filming the remainder of *Avatar 4* until after the release of *Avatar: Fire and Ash*.[[11]](#cite_note-11) In November 2025, Cameron said the next two sequels would not be produced if *Fire and Ash* was unsuccessful at the box office, but that he "will write a book" instead to resolve the "one open thread" the third installment leaves open.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

A fifth film has been announced and is scheduled for December 19, 2031.[[7]](#cite_note-D'Alessandro-7) It is currently planned to be the final film of the franchise.[[13]](#cite_note-13) Jon Landau stated that part of *Avatar 5* will take place on Earth, with Neytiri visiting the planet.[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15)[[7]](#cite_note-D'Alessandro-7)[[8]](#cite_note-varietyreleasedates-8) Cameron stated that *Avatar: The Quest for Eywa* is being considered as a possible title for the film.[[16]](#cite_note-titleleaks-16)[[17]](#cite_note-Keegan-17)[[18]](#cite_note-faroutmagazine.co.uk-18)

Cameron said he would consider making sixth and seventh films if there was demand for them. However, he said that due to his age and the complexity of making *Avatar* films, he would have to train a successor to produce them.[[17]](#cite_note-Keegan-17)

President of Columbia University :: President's House :: chunk_0004
Main article: [President's House (Columbia University)](/wiki/President%27s_House_(Columbia_University) "President's House (Columbia University)")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/ColumbiaPresidentsHouseold.jpg/250px-ColumbiaPresidentsHouseold.jpg)](/wiki/File:ColumbiaPresidentsHouseold.jpg)

The President's House (1862–1897) at Columbia's Midtown campus

At Columbia's midtown Manhattan campus (1857–1896), a house for the president was built in 1862 near the corner of 49th Street and [Fourth Avenue](/wiki/Park_Avenue "Park Avenue") (later Park Avenue), which served as the home of both Charles King and Frederick Augustus Porter Barnard. It was the president's official residence until that campus' demolition in 1897.

The current house for the president of Columbia University, located on the university's [Morningside Heights](/wiki/Morningside_Heights "Morningside Heights") campus, was built in 1912, and has served as the official residence of the university president since, with the exception of during the tenure of Michael Sovern, who chose to instead continue living in his Upper East Side apartment. The house was reoccupied upon the accession of George Rupp in 1993, and has remained in use since then.[[54]](#cite_note-78)

Demolition of the building was considered as late as 1991,[[55]](#cite_note-79) though the building underwent a comprehensive renovation in 2005.[[56]](#cite_note-80)
